risk_assessment.rationale: The message is flagged as phishing (MITRE ATT&CK T1566) and originates from IP 52.14.201.94 and domain printhub‑sg.com, both of which have no known reputation. The risk assessment is medium severity with medium confidence.

recommended_actions: Escalate to a human analyst for manual review
recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Initiate a deeper forensic review of the original Mimecast quarantine payload (including full headers, attachment hashes, and any embedded URLs) to confirm whether malicious code or credential‑phishing content is present.

Run the sender IP (52.14.201.94) through multiple threat intel platforms (e.g., VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, GreyNoise) and request a passive DNS lookup for printhub-sg.com to uncover any historical abuse that may not be reflected in current reputation feeds.

Create a temporary block or sinkhole rule for the domain printhub-sg.com and its associated IP range on your perimeter firewalls and email gateways while the investigation is ongoing, but keep an audit trail so you can quickly lift it if the domain proves benign.

Contact the purported sender (admin@victimcorp.com) via a verified internal channel to verify whether they actually initiated a support ticket with that reference number; if not, treat the message as spoofed and inform the user base of the attempted phishing campaign.

Log the full email content (including any URLs or attachments) into your secure incident‑response repository and share it with relevant threat‑sharing communities (e.g., ISACs, MISP) to aid collective detection.

If a malicious payload is confirmed, execute endpoint containment procedures on any workstation that may have opened the message—run an EDR scan, isolate the host, and reset potentially compromised credentials.
Update your email security policies to flag similar bulk‑phishing patterns (subject line “Ticket #* has been resolved”) with higher severity in future detections.
triage_rationale_experimental: The message was blocked as bulk phishing and originates from an unknown sender domain/IP, but without concrete evidence of malicious content or victim interaction the true intent cannot be definitively confirmed.
